title: EXAMINING THE CHANGE IN SECONDARY SCHOOL STUDENTS' AWARENESS OF GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE
abstract: Educational institutions play a vital role in fostering effective, informed citizens who are knowledgeable about national and global issues. Social studies is a program that aims to fulfil this role. This study examines changes in secondary school students’ awareness of global climate change in the context of social responsibility activities. In this context, social studies teacher candidates were given training on social responsibility and global climate change; activities were designed and social responsibility initiatives were carried out collaboratively by the faculty and the school. This mixedmethods study employs a concurrent nested design. This design emphasizes qualitative studies. In this study, conducted in Izmir province with 27 secondary school students and 10 social studies teacher candidates, the scale was administered experimentally only to the secondary school students in a pre- and post-test format and analysed using SPSS. For the qualitative component, data obtained from all participants through interviews, open-ended questionnaires, worksheets, observations, and focus group interviews were analysed using descriptive and content analyses. title: PROMOTING WORKPLACE INDEPENDENCE IN INDIVIDUALS WITH AUTISM USING VIDEO MODELING
abstract: This study examined the effectiveness of video modeling for teaching office-cleaning skills to individuals with autism. The targeted skills included (a) preparing the office for cleaning, (b) dusting and wiping office materials, and (c) mopping the office floor. A multiple-baseline design across participants was used to evaluate changes in independent task performance across baseline, intervention, and follow-up phases. Instruction was delivered via systematically developed video models demonstrating each step of the cleaning routines. Performance data were collected using task analyses and were analyzed by visual inspection and effect-size calculations. In addition, acquisition of non-targeted information related to the target skills was assessed. The findings showed that video modeling led to marked improvements in participants’ independent, accurate completion of office cleaning tasks. Furthermore, the acquired skills were maintained over time and generalized across different office settings and materials. Social validity data indicated positive perceptions among both participants and their parents. Overall, the results support video modeling as an effective, evidence based inst

title: COMPARISON OF SOCIAL STUDIES TEACHER CANDIDATES’ PERCEPTIONS OF LOCAL HISTORY IN MALATYA WITH OTHER CITIES
abstract: In social studies curricula, skills, values, learning outcomes, and areas of learning related to the discipline of history are incorporated with due consideration for students’ developmental characteristics. The training process and readiness levels of teachers—who play a key role in conveying this content to students—are crucial because they influence their professional competence. In the transmission of this content, which follows a path from the near to the far, from the known to the unknown, and from the local to the universal, students are first expected to recognize and make sense of the place where they live. For this reason, the transmission of local history content to students is valuable for the realization of the targeted learning outcomes. To determine the sensitivity of prospective teachers and foster their awareness, it is important to conduct certain studies on local history at the undergraduate level. To this end, and for the purposes of this study, the opinions of a 40-member study group were sought, consisting of first-, second-, third-, and fourth-year students enrolled in the Social Studies Teaching undergraduateprogram at the Faculty of Education, Inönü Univers

title: THE USE OF THE SOCRATIC METHOD IN VISUAL PERCEPTION TRAINING AND ITS EFFECTS ON PRIMARY SCHOOL STUDENTS’ DRAWINGS
abstract: Drawing, one of the most fundamental ways children express themselves, varies with age. Students in the study group, who are developmentally in the concrete operational stage, occasionally use templates in their drawings. In this context, the Socratic method, aimed at activating cognitive processes through guided questioning rather than presenting direct answers, emerges as a prominent approach, holding significant potential for the development of visual perception. This study aims to examine the effect of the Socratic method used in visual perception training on the self-portrait drawings of fourth-grade primary school students. The study employed one-group pretest–posttest weak experimental design, one of the quantitative research methods. The study group consisted of 55 fourth-grade primary school students. The data were obtained by evaluating the students’ self-portraits drawn before and after the implementation of the Socratic method, using the SelfPortrait Evaluation Rubric. Inter-rater reliability had been established for the data, and a pairedsamples t-test was used for the analysis. title: PARENT BULLYING TOWARD TEACHERS IN PRIVATE SCHOOLS
abstract: The aim of this study is to examine parent bullying experienced by teachers working in private schools based on teachers’ perspectives and to reveal the forms and content of these experiences. The study was designed within the framework of the qualitative research approach, and the study group consisted of teachers employed in private schools. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using content analysis. The findings revealed that teachers experience parent bullying in various forms, including questioning professional competence, grade-related pressure, intimidation and complaints as means of exerting pressure, the use of institutional authority, and acts of discrediting. The results indicate that parent bullying is not merely an individual communication problem but rather a structural phenomenon associated with the redistribution of power relations within the context of private schools. The marketization of education in line with neoliberal policies and the positioning of parents in power through economic capital weaken teachers’ pedagogical autonomy and make symbolic forms of pressure more visible. title: THE EFFECT OF A CLIENT HOLISTIC ASSESSMENT TRAINING PROGRAM ON THE SKILLS OF PSYCHOLOGICAL COUNSELOR CANDIDATES IN THE FIRST INTERVIEW
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of the Client Holistic Assessment Training Program on preservicepsychological counselors’ perceptions of their holistic assessment competencies. The study was conducted using a quasi-experimental design. The research group consisted of 20 psychologicalcounseling candidates, with 10 participants assigned to the control group and 10 to the experimentalgroup. The average age of the participants is 22.7. Twelve of the participants are women, and eightare men. The experimental and control groups were formed based on the participants’ pre-test scores. Data were collected using the Personal Information Form and the Holistic Client Assessment Competency Scale. The experimental group received a 10-session Holistic Client Assessment Training Program, whereas the control group received no intervention. The study’s findings indicate that participants in the experimental group showed a significant increase in their perceived holistic assessment competencies across all subdimensions. Effect sizes were reported using the r statistic. In the final cross-group comparisons, large effects were observed for the subscales Initial Therapeutic Relationship (ITR), Inf

title: AN INVESTIGATION INTO THE ATTITUDES OF ART EDUCATION STUDENTS TOWARDS DIGITALIZATION IN TERMS OF VARIOUS VARIABLES
abstract: his study aims to examine the relationship between the Digital Citizenship Levels (DCL) and Attitudes Towards Digital Technology (ATDT) of art education students. The research was conducted using the relational survey model, one of the descriptive methods. The study group consists of a total of 322 undergraduate students (191 female, 131 male) studying in the Department of Art Education at various universities. A Personal Information Form, the Attitude Scale Towards Digital Technology (ASTDT), and the Digital Citizenship Scale (DCS) were utilized as data collection tools. For data analysis, t-test, ANOVA, and the Tukey test for post-hoc significant differences were applied based on variables such as gender, grade level, income status, and duration of internet usage (at a significance level of p < .05 and a 95% confidence interval). As a result of the correlation analysis conducted between DCL and ATDT, a moderate significant relationship was found between the two variables (p < .05). title: ACADEMIC PROCRASTINATION AND FOMO THE MEDIATING ROLE OF CAREER STRESS
abstract: This study examines the mediating role of career stress in the relationship between university students’ academic procrastination and fear of missing out (FoMO) regarding social media updates. In this context, research data were collected from 449 university students who volunteered to participate in the study. The research data were collected using the Academic Procrastination Scale, the Fear of Missing Out (FoMO) Scale on social media, and the Career Stress Scale. For the analysis of demographic data within the scope of the research, frequencies, percentages, and mean scores were obtained. Tests for normality were performed, and the dataset met the normality assumption. Pearson’s correlation coefficient was used to calculate correlations between variables. The PROCESS macro add-in was used to test whether career stress mediates the relationship between academic procrastination and fear of missing out (FoMO) on social media. The findings reveal positive and significant relationships among academic procrastination, fear of missing out, and career stress. title: NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS AWARENESS AMONG PRE-SERVICE TEACHERS IN TÜRKİYE: DEVELOPMENTAL LANGUAGE DISORDER REMAINS UNDER-RECOGNISED
abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD), such as attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and specific learning disorder (SLD), are increasingly recognised, yet awareness of developmental language disorder (DLD) and of its former term, specific language impairment (SLI), remains limited. This study examined awareness, knowledge sources, and perceptions of six NDDs among pre-service teachers at two universities in Türkiye. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in spring 2025 with 466 participants from Mersin and Anadolu Universities. Descriptive statistics and paired-sample proportion tests were used to compare DLD awareness with that of other conditions. Results showed that ADHD (82.2%) and ASD (69.5%) were the most recognised, while DLD (23.8%) and SLI (4.3%) were the least recognised. Although some participants reported awareness, most definitions were inaccurate, revealing misconceptions. The media were the primary source of awareness, whereas personal connections had minimal influence. DLD (1.3%) and SLI (1.1%) were rarely selected as the most prevalent NDDs. title: PRINCIPAL ETHICAL LEADERSHIP SCALE: A VALIDITY AND RELIABILITY STUDY BASED ON TEACHERS’ PERCEPTIONS
abstract: Ethical leadership is a critical dimension of leadership, particularly in educational settings, where the moral climate, trust, and professional relationships within schools are influenced by leaders. Although the body of research on ethical leadership in Türkiye has expanded in recent years, there remains a persistent need for valid and reliable measurement instruments that enable cross-cultural and international comparisons. This study aims to adapt the Ethical Leadership Questionnaire (ELQ), originally developed by Yukl et al. (2013), into Turkish within the context of school principals and to examine its validity and reliability based on teachers’ perceptions. The study was conducted with twoindependent samples of teachers (N=152 and N=153) from different types of schools in Malatya. The adaptation process followed standard procedures, including translation, back-translation, expert review, and linguistic validation. Construct validity was examined through Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), while reliability was assessed using internal consistency coefficients. title: CONTEMPORARY FOUNDATIONS OF THE TÜRKIYE CENTURY MAARIF MODEL
abstract: The Türkiye Century Maarif Model (TCMM) is among the most debated educational restructuringinitiatives in the history of the Republic. Debates surrounding the model generally focus on two claims: that it is insufficiently national and that it compromises contemporaneity. This study addresses the second criticism by examining the contemporary foundations of the TCMM curricula. Within this framework, the K–12 Skills Framework, the Holistic Paradigm, literacy skills, and instructional differentiation are discussed in terms of their definitions, scope, and theoretical foundations. The analysis indicates that the TCMM curricula are grounded in 21st-century skills increasingly prioritized by countries shaping global education and economies, including the United States, European Union members, and Canada, as well as by international organizations such as the OECD, UNICEF, and UNESCO. International assessments that influence educational policy, including PISA, TIMSS, and PIRLS, also reflect this orientation. These skills are closely associated with major dynamics of the contemporary era, such as Industry 4.0, machine learning and robotics, digital citizenship, and Education/Pedagogy 4.0. B

title: ARTISTIC EXPRESSIONS OF VISUAL ARTS TEACHER CANDIDATES CONCERNING THE IMAGE OF WOMAN: AN A/R/TOGRAPHIC INQUIRY
abstract: The image of woman has been an important symbol in aesthetic production as both a normative and narrative figure. Social developments and innovations have also interpreted, positioned, and assigned various ideological roles to this image. This study aims to examine visual arts teacher candidates’ perspectives on the image of woman and how these perspectives are transformed into artistic expression. The study focuses on the a/r/tographic processes carried out with students in the Department of Art Education within the “Elective Studio” course during the spring semester of 2020–2021. Within the framework of a/r/tography, a rhizomatic analysis approach was adopted. Through the activities, the participants’ perceptions, interpretations, associations, and experiences related to the image of woman were examined. Data obtained from interviews, reflective writings, and visual productions were analyzed under the theme of “Form.” In this process, the categories of “Masculine Form” and “Feminine Form” emerged. title: THE EFFECT OF DIGITAL WRITING APPLICATIONS ON 9TH-GRADE STUDENTS’ WRITING ATTITUDES
abstract: This study examined the effect of digital writing activities on 9th-grade students’ attitudes toward writing and described the characteristics of student products created in digital environments. Thestudy used an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design. In the quantitative phase, a quasiexperimental pretest-posttest control-group design was used; in the qualitative phase, studentproducts were examined using document and content analyses. The participants were 59 ninthgradestudents studying at a science high school in Türkiye, with 30 students in the experimental group and 29 students in the control group. The experimental group completed a five-week digital writing program that included e-story, e-poem, e-fairy tale, e-essay, and e-mail writing activities. The “Paper-to-Digital Writing Attitude Scale” was used to measure students’ attitudes toward writing in paper-based and digital environments; therefore, the quantitative results were interpreted in relation to writing attitude rather than as a direct measurement of creativity or self-confidence. Quantitative data were analyzed using the Shapiro-Wilk normality test, independent samples t-test, and paired samples t-test. The qu

title: A NEW LABORATORY PRACTICE FOR IMPROVING REASONING SKILLS AND ACHIEVEMENT
abstract: Reasoning skills play an important role in overcoming difficult problems in geometry. Therefore, the aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of a new laboratory application integrating physical and technological contents on the development of Reasoning Skills (RS) and Geometry Achievement (GA). The study was designed according to a mixed-type, pretest-posttest control group true experimental design. The study was conducted with 52 students in the experimental group where laboratory interventions were applied and 50 students in the control group where no intervention was applied. The experimental implementation lasted fifteen weeks. The study data were collected with the Reasoning Skills on Geometric Shapes (RSGS) Test and the Interview Form (IF) together with the GA test. Quantitative data were analyzed using paired samples t-test, analysis of covariance and Benferroni test, and qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis. The results showed that the post-test scores of the RSGS and the GA differed significantly between the experimental and control groups in favor of the experimental group. title: DIGITAL LITERACY IN TURKISH LANGUAGE COURSE MATERIALS UNDER THE MAARIF MODEL
abstract: This study aims to explore the extent to which digital literacy components are embedded in the 5th-grade Turkish language arts curriculum and textbook developed under the Türkiye Century Maarif Model (TCMM), as well as how these components are represented in terms of content. Digital literacy is defined as a core competency area encompassing multidimensional skills such as accessing information in digital environments, content creation, critical evaluation, ethical use, and collaborative digital production. Accordingly, this study employed document analysis to investigate both the curriculum and the textbook, and the data were thematically analyzed based on seven digital literacy components: digital access to information, media literacy, digital content creation, critical digital evaluation, digital ethics and safety, digital collaboration, and conceptual awareness. The findings revealed that the curriculum addressed digital literacy components in a multifaceted manner; however, the textbook primarily focused on access to information and media literacy. title: PREDICTORS OF THE DARK TRIAD PERSONALITY: PER-CEIVED PARENTING STYLES AND CHILDHOOD TRAU-MAS
abstract: Recent studies show that childhood traumas are associated with difficulties in emotional regulation, which, in turn, have been linked to the development of the dark triad personality traits. The dark triadis associated with emotional dysregulation, interpersonal problems, and aggression. Furthermore, family and parental attitudes during childhood are associated with personality and psychologicalwell-being. This demonstrates the importance of childhood experiences. This study aims to examinethe extent to which parental attitudes and childhood traumas predict the dark triad in university students and to investigate gender differences. The study employed a correlational (cross-sectional)survey design, and participants were recruited through convenience sampling. The study included410 students from a state university in the eastern region of Türkiye (Hakkari University) (male: 46.34%; female: 53.66%). The relationships between university students’ dark triad personality traits, perceived parental attitudes, and childhood traumas were analysed using Pearson correlations, simple linear regressions, and independent-samples t-tests. title: MAPPING THE EARLY IDENTIFICATION LITERATURE ON GIFTEDNESS: A BIBLIOMETRIC STUDY
abstract: This study aims to examine the intellectual structure, conceptual orientations, and temporal development of the international literature on the early identification of gifted children through a bibliometric approach. The dataset comprises 77 articles published between 1969 and January 2025 in the Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection; all focus on early identification. Data were collected through a systematic search of the WoS database, and bibliometric techniques were employed to analyze publication trends, country and institutional productivity, citation patterns, author collaborations, and thematic structures based on keyword co-occurrence. The findings reveal a notable increase in scientific output on early identification, particularly after 2007, with an average annual growth rate of 2.92%. Country-level analysis indicates that the United States leads in scientific impact, while institutions such as the University of Ioannina and Aristotle University of Thessaloniki lead in productivity. title: THE EFFECT OF THE “CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT IN GIFTED EDUCATION” COURSE ON PRE-SERVICE TEACHERS’ ATTITUDES TOWARD GIFTED EDUCATION
abstract: This study examines the attitudes of pre-service special education teachers toward the education of gifted individuals and evaluates the effect of the “Curriculum Development in Gifted Education” course on these attitudes. Designed as an experimental study, it used a one-group pretest–posttest design. Forty-two pre-service teachers enrolled in the Special Education Department of Nevşehir Hacı Bektaş Veli University during the 2024–2025 academic year participated. The “Attitude Scale Regarding the Education of the Gifted” (ÜYETÖ) was administered as a pretest at the start of the course and re-administered as a posttest at the end of the 14-week course. The data were evaluated using difference analysis for dependent groups and repeated-measures MANOVA. The findings showed that the pre-service teachers already held generally positive attitudes toward the education of the gifted before the course, but that these attitudes strengthened significantly afterward. Statistically significant increases were observed particularly in the “Needs and Support for the Gifted,” “Establishing Special Talent Classes,” and “Grade Skipping” sub-dimensions. title: AN EXAMINATION OF PRE-SERVICE MIDDLE SCHOOL MATHEMATICS TEACHERS’ VIEWS ON REASONING
abstract: Reasoning is one of the most fundamental skills required for learning and doing mathematics. It is therefore important to determine how mathematics teachers, who are responsible for the development of their students’ reasoning skills, approach reasoning. The aim of this study is to examine pre-service middle school mathematics teachers’ views on reasoning. This qualitative descriptive study involved 61 senior-year pre-service middle school mathematics teachers. Views on Reasoning Form, developed by the researchers was administered to the participants, and the data obtained were analyzed using content analysis. The participants most frequently viewed reasoning as a process and as problem solving. In the examples of reasoning related to daily life and mathematics, the participants generally did not explicitly demonstrate their reasoning processes. Deductive reasoning was used most frequently in the examples related to daily life and mathematics. In addition, arithmetic reasoning was least common in the daily-life examples, whereas algebraic and probabilistic reasoning were least common in the mathematics examples. title: PERCEIVED IMPACT OF USING SOCIAL MEDIA AS AN ARTISTIC PORTFOLIO ON MOTIVATION
abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the perceived impact of undergraduate students’ use of socialmedia as artistic portfolios on their motivation in the Department of Art Education, Division of Painting Education at a state university in Ankara. The study included 24 second-, third-, and fourthyearstudents during the 2025–2026 academic year. Using a qualitative research approach, data were collected through an open-ended questionnaire and semi-structured interviews and analyzed using descriptive analysis. The study focused on the social media platform Instagram. The findings indicate that social media is actively used by students for creating artistic portfolios, digital archiving, and ensuring professional visibility. Senior students evaluate the platform more strategically with respect to job opportunities, whereas junior students use it more for inspiration and exploration. The effect of social media on motivation was found to be twofold: while constructive feedback, visibility, and a sense of belonging support artistic production, factors such as like-related anxiety, social comparison, and algorithmic influences may lead to feelings of inadequacy and psychological distress. title: Challenges Faced by Supervisors in Inspection and Guidance Activities in Quran Courses from the Perspective of Non-Formal Religious Education
abstract: Inspection and guidance in educational institutions play a vital role in enhancing quality, efficiency and success as indispensable elements of management. In this context, Quran courses, key providers of non-formal religious education, are inspected by the Presidency of Religious Affairs (DIB) through structured guidance and inspection activities. Inspector (Murakıp), working under mufti offices, execute these programs while also taking part in investigation and in-service training processes. Today, increasing demand for these courses has led to diversified curricula, making effective inspection even more critical. This study investigates the alignment of current inspection practices with modern educational standards and institutional needs. It aims to identify systemic deficiencies and provide concrete solutions for improvement. Designed as a qualitative case study, the research employed MAXQDA-supported content analysis. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 18 murakıps in Istanbul to gain deep insights into the challenges faced during inspection and guidance processes in Quran courses. title: Exploring Pre-Service Teachers’ Professional Perceptions Through Media
abstract: This study aims to explore the professional perceptions of senior pre-service science teachers through news on the teaching profession. Participants in this phenomenological study were selected using convenience and criterion sampling methods. In the data collection process, participants were first asked to select professional news that caught their attention in the media; then, their feelings and thoughts regarding the news that attracted the most attention were identified. The findings reveal that participants mostly interested in news themed around career planning, performance, violence, economic conditions and educational practices. Participants evaluated 68% of the news they shared as negative. It was found that participants experienced emotions such as sadness, anger, fear and surprise in response to news about appointment quotas, the interview process, the National Education Academy, violence against teachers and insufficient salaries. In contrast, they exhibited positive emotions such as joy, confidence and hope in response to news presenting teachers’ success stories. title: The Mediating Role of Psychological Resilience in the Socio-Cultural Adaptation and Spiritual Well-Being of International Students
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the mediating role of psychological resilience in the relationship between sociocultural adaptation and spiritual well-being among international students who came to Turkey for undergraduate education. The research method employed is a correlational survey model, a type of quantitative research design. The study sample consisted of 294 (187 female, 107 male) international undergraduate students enrolled at universities in Turkey. The data collection instruments used in the study were a Personal Information Form, the Sociocultural Adaptation Scale, the Brief Resilience Scale, and the Three-Factor Spiritual Well-Being Scale. Relationships between variables were examined using Pearson Correlation Analysis. The mediating role of psychological resilience in the relationship between spirituality and socio-cultural adaptation was analyzed using PROCESS v3.4 (Model 4) developed by Hayes. title: Bibliometric Analysis of Research on Critical and Creative Thinking in Education
abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the research conducted in the field of education on critical and creative thinking in the context of skills, abilities, and competencies, and to carry out a bibliometric analysis of these studies. In line with this aim, a bibliometric analysis was conducted based on the articles retrieved from the Web of Science database on March 9, 2025, using the keywords (“creative thinking” AND “critical thinking”) AND (“skills” OR “abilities” OR “competencies”). The studies obtained from the search were subjected to specific criteria, and as a result, a bibliometric analysis was carried out with 149 articles. The R-Studio software was used to conduct the bibliometric analyses. Within the scope of the study, the distribution of research on critical and creative thinking by years, the most prolific authors and journals, the citation status of authors and countries, international collaboration networks, and prominent themes were examined. The results indicate that academic production in this field has accelerated over the past ten years and that studies are more intensively conducted in certain countries. title: Developing Screen Use Scales for Mothers and 4-5-Year-Old Children
abstract: This study aimed to develop two valid and reliable measurement tools to determine the screen use of 4- and 5-year-old preschool children and their mothers. The construct validity of the scales was tested using exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis. The reliability of the scales was measured using Cronbach's alpha reliability coefficient, item-total score correlation, and a discrimination test for the lower 27%. The study was conducted with 382 4- and 5-year-old children and their mothers attending kindergartens in a province in the Eastern Anatolia Region during the 2024-2025 academic year. As a result of the exploratory factor analysis, it was determined that the tool measuring mothers' screen use consisted of 6 factors and 24 items, while the tool measuring children's screen use consisted of 3 factors and 17 items. The structures emerging from the exploratory factor analysis were confirmed by confirmatory factor analysis. In the reliability analysis of the scales, the Cronbach's alpha reliability coefficient was determined to be .844 for the instrument measuring mothers' screen use and .845 for the instrument measuring children's screen use. title: The Relationship Between Students’ Complex Problem Posing and Story Writing Skills
abstract: This study was conducted to determine the relationship between sixth-grade intermediate school students' free story writing skills and complex problem posing skills. A mixed method design was used to investigate this issue in a more holistic manner. The participants of the study were consisted of 217 sixth-grade students from an intermediate school in Province X, selected through a convenience sampling method. A free story writing form and two different semi-structured problem posing forms were used to collect data from the participants. The study determined that the students posed a total of 1983 problems based on two different semi-structured problem posing situations. After the analysis of them, they were classified as unsolvable and solvable mathematical problems, not problems. Solvable mathematical problems were analyzed and identified as homework, relational, and conditional problems. Participants posed the most problems in the homework category and the least problems in the relational problem category. title: Temperament as a Mediator Between Parental Anxiety and Child Mental Health
abstract: Parental anxiety has consistently been associated with adverse child outcomes, yet the mechanisms linking parental distress to child mental health remain underexplored, particularly in non-Western settings. This study examined whether child temperament - specifically, cautious and high-maintenance profiles - mediates the relationship between parental anxiety and children’s emotional and behavioral difficulties within a Turkish sample. Participants were 606 parents (91.7% mothers) of children aged 6 to 12 years (M = 7.86, SD = 2.24). Parents completed an online survey including the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale (DASS-21) to assess parental anxiety, the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) for child mental health, and the School-Age Temperament Inventory (SATI) to measure child temperament. Sociodemographic variables were also collected and statistically controlled. Data were analyzed using Hayes’ PROCESS macro (Model 4). Results showed that parental anxiety significantly predicted both child temperament and mental health outcomes. title: Examining Pre-service Teachers’ Awareness of Global Climate Change Using a Mixed-method Approach
abstract: Global climate change is recognized as one of the most significant environmental problems of today, and training pre-service teachers who are aware of this issue is crucial for fostering environmental consciousness in society. Therefore, this study examined pre-service teachers’ awareness of global climate change and the factors influencing it. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, the study employed a correlational survey model in the quantitative phase and a phenomenological design in the qualitative phase. The research was conducted with 978 pre-service teachers studying in science, primary, and social studies education programs during the 2022–2023 academic year. Quantitative data were analyzed through descriptive statistical methods, while qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis. The findings revealed that pre-service teachers had generally high levels of awareness of global climate change. Awareness was very high regarding the effects on the natural and human environment and energy consumption, but lower in relation to global organizations and the causes of climate change. title: Reading Anxiety and Difficulties of Syrian Students in Turkish Reading
abstract: This study examined the Turkish course‐related and reading anxiety, as well as the reading difficulties, of Syrian students attending primary schools in Turkey. Data were collected from 395 students using the Turkish Course Anxiety Scale (TDKÖ) and the Turkish Reading Anxiety Scale (TOKÖ). According to the analysis results, while a significant difference was found in communication anxiety by gender (p = .021), no difference was observed in overall anxiety levels (p = .580). As grade level increased, Turkish course anxiety (p = .005), test anxiety (p = .010), and fear of negative evaluation (p = .035) decreased; similarly, reading anxiety differed by both gender (p = .037) and grade level (p = .002). In addition, a moderate relationship was identified between Turkish course anxiety and reading anxiety (r = .566, p < .01), and a significantly high negative relationship was found between reading anxiety and Turkish reading achievement (p < .001). The results indicate that the anxieties experienced by Syrian students interact with their learning processes. Therefore, support programs should be implemented to reduce students' anxieties.

title: The Effect of Cyber Dating Abuse on Self-Esteem and Achievement-Oriented Motivation
abstract: The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of cyber dating abuse on self-esteem and achievement-oriented motivation. With the widespread use of social media all over the world, new forms of socialization and communication have emerged. The recent increase in the use of messaging platforms such as WhatsApp, tools that provide instant communication, and social media channels such as Facebook has caused interpersonal relationships to gain importance and brought the issue of cyber dating abuse to the agenda as one of the current problems of recent years. When looking at the literature, it is seen that research on the factors associated with cyber dating abuse is quite limited. Findings will be obtained regarding the effects of individuals' level of exposure to cyber dating abuse on their self-esteem and academic motivation. According to the results obtained, it was seen that the level of exposure to cyber dating abuse had a statistically significant positive relationship with self-esteem and a statistically significant negative relationship with success-oriented motivation. title: A Cross-National Comparison of Nomination Criteria for Gifted Individuals: A PRISMA-Based Systematic Review
abstract: This study provides a comparative examination of nomination processes for gifted students across different countries. In order to reveal how identification criteria vary internationally, a systematic literature review was conducted in line with the PRISMA 2020 protocol. Out of 1,242 studies retrieved from the SCOPUS, ERIC, Web of Science, and ULAKBİM databases, 53 were included in the analysis based on eligibility criteria. The data obtained through document analysis were thematically coded, resulting in the identification of 13 nomination criteria. The study examined the identification systems of 29 countries in detail and analyzed similarities and differences through these criteria. Findings indicate that the most frequently used criteria are teacher nomination, parental input, and academic achievement, while in some countries multiple measures such as intelligence tests, psychological evaluations, portfolios, and creative thinking are also employed. Asian countries tend to adopt more systematic and centralized approaches, whereas Western European countries favor more flexible, individually oriented application models. title: A Systematic Review of Graduate Theses on Inclusive Education in Turkey
abstract: This study aims to examine master's and doctoral theses on inclusive education conducted within the national literature. The research employed the document analysis method, a qualitative research approach that enables the systematic examination of graduate theses. The data source consisted of 70 theses registered in the National Thesis Center system. Theses were selected through criterion sampling, one of the purposeful sampling methods, by including those conducted in the field of education and instruction. Data were analyzed using content analysis based on a thesis review form developed according to the research questions. The findings revealed that 2023 was the year with the highest number of studies at both the master's and doctoral levels. Most theses were prepared in the Department of Classroom Education (n=15). The qualitative method (n=33) was the most preferred, while the mixed-method (n=15) was the least used. The majority of studies (n=49) were conducted with teachers, and the most common data collection tools were interviews (n=38) and scales (n=24). title: Biomimicry-Based Design Solutions to Everyday Life Problems by 5th Grade Middle School Students
abstract: The aim of this study is to have middle school students solve a problem they have determined from daily life by getting inspiration from the structures of the living beings they have chosen and to develop original designs for this solution. The sample of the study consisted of 19 fifth grade students, 9 girls and 10 boys, studying in a village school. The students divided into 10 groups of 2 or 3 people and each group asked to draw their own designs. The nature trip observation sheet and the design process evaluation survey consisting of open-ended questions were used as data collection tools. The obtained data were analyzed using content analysis. It was seen that the students were inspired by 9 different living beings to solve a problem they determined from daily life with their group friends. The drawings made by the students were collected in 4 different categories as “protection”, “clothing”, security”, and “cleaning”. When the designs of the student groups examined, it has seen that they generally imitated the structures and functions of the living beings they were inspired by. title: The Role of Literacy Types in Societal Development
abstract: In the 21st century, the significance of various literacy types has become increasingly evident in individuals’ social lives. Literacy types, which are aimed to be acquired from primary school onward throughout formal education, are deliberately selected and emphasized in educational programs. Each country includes different types of literacies in its curriculum, and as curricula are updated, new literacy types emerge in response to evolving societal needs. In this context, the 2024 Turkish Language Curriculum published by the Turkish Ministry of National Education outlines ten target literacy competencies. This study aims to examine these literacies—namely information, digital, financial, visual, cultural, citizenship, data, sustainability, artistic, and systems literacy—as presented in the 2024 Turkish Language Curriculum, and to identify their potential social impact. In line with this aim, findings were obtained for each grade level (5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th). The inclusion of literacy types in the curriculum and the selection of intended literacies were evaluated to derive implications for the Turkish education system. title: University Students’ Experiences with Distance and Face-to-Face Education After The February 6th Earthquakes
abstract: As a result of the Kahramanmaraş earthquakes on 6 February 2023, over 50,000 people lost their lives and hundreds of thousands were forced to leave their homes. Education was also severely affected by the earthquake, which has been described as the disaster of the century. Universities initially suspended education, and subsequently, universities in the province of Kahramanmaraş decided to switch from face-to-face to distance learning, and Distance learning has lasted for more than a year. This research aimed to examine the effects of this transition from in-person to distance learning from the students' perspective. The study was conducted using a phenomenological design within the framework of qualitative research paradigms. Data was collected through structured interview forms and subjected to thematic analysis. Fifteen individuals were interviewed face-to-face, and seven different themes were identified: "Disadvantages of Distance Learning," "Advantages of Distance Learning," "Environmental Conditions," "Searching for Solutions," "Attitudes of Academics," "Motivation for In-Person Education," and "Choosing Teaching Methods." title: Bullying and Temperament in Preschool Children: The Role of Parents’ Emotional Socialization Practices
abstract: This study examined the effects of parents’ emotional socialization attitudes on children’s bullying and victim behaviors as well as temperament traits within the context of demographic variables. The findings revealed that parents’ distress, punitive, minimizing, and emotion-focused responses play a decisive role in children’s social and emotional development. In particular, punitive and minimizing parental reactions were associated with negative temperament traits and bullying behaviors, while emotion-focused responses were found to increase victimization tendencies. Moreover, factors such as children’s gender, age, parents’ education level, and socio-economic status significantly influenced parental attitudes and children’s temperament characteristics. Accordingly, the study demonstrates that the quality of emotional communication within the family directly affects children’s social behaviors. The way parents respond to emotions shapes how children build relationships with themselves and with others. title: Process-Based Therapy: A Personalized Paradigm in Psychotherapy
abstract: Process-Based Therapy (PBT) has emerged as a holistic and individualized psychotherapy model that addresses individuals’ psychosocial needs based on biopsychosocial processes, overcoming the limitations of traditional symptom-focused approaches. Its primary goal is to enhance psychological flexibility, enabling individuals to develop more adaptive responses to environmental challenges. In this context, PBT focuses on the core processes that shape individual functioning rather than specific symptom clusters and draws on theoretical frameworks such as the Extended Evolutionary Meta-Model (EEMM) to make sense of these processes. This review comprehensively examines the theoretical foundations, historical development, and clinical applications of PBT, while also exploring recent advancements and process-based assessment approaches in the literature. In particular, it highlights the role of assessment tools such as the Process-Based Assessment Tool (PBAT) in evaluating therapeutic processes and monitoring treatment effectiveness. title: Pre-service Teachers’ Perceptions of Future Education
abstract: The aim of this research is to reveal pre-service teachers’ perceptions of how students, teachers, parents, schools, and the education system will evolve in the future. The research was conducted using a qualitative research design, specifically phenomenology. Maximum diversity sampling, a type of purposeful sampling, was used to determine the study group. The study group consists of a total of 111 students studying in different departments of the Faculty of Education at Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam University. Research data were collected using a document form and a semi-structured interview form, and content analysis was used to analyse the data. According to the results, it was determined that students are expected to possess positive characteristics in the future, such as being technologically proficient, inquisitive, research-oriented, having learned how to learn, problemsolving, curious, sceptical, creative, active, self-controlled, and respectful of differences. In terms of negative characteristics, it was determined that students are expected to experience a decline in critical and creative thinking, problems with focus, and a lack of motivation towards school in the future. title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in K-12 Education: Bibliometric Analysis and Trends
abstract: The aim of this research is to identify trends, general tendencies, and collaboration networks in generative AI research at the K-12 level. The Web of Science database was searched for research on generative AI and education, and 207 studies were included. The research included the most productive and most cited authors, institutions, and countries in the field, as well as analysis of collaboration networks and thematic analysis. Biblioshniy, an R Studio program, was used for data analysis. The research found that China and the US are at the center of generative AI research at the K-12 level, while cross-national collaboration networks are weak. Institutionally, institutions based in China, the US, Hong Kong, and Australia are leading institutions. The most published journals are high-impact journals in the field of educational technologies. Trending topics within the field include generative AI, technological pedagogical domain knowledge, computational thinking skills, artificial intelligence literacy, self-regulation skills, assessment, ChatGPT, teacher education, curriculum integration, skills, obstacles, and opportunities. title: The Mediating Role of Meaningful Living Between Desperation and Boredom and Self-Transcendence
abstract: Positive and negative experiences happen in life. Reactions to situations and feelings experienced are also influenced by events, personal, and environmental factors. In an event that is evaluatedbased on such factors and from which there seems to be no escape, one may feel desperation and experience boredom. The purpose of this study was to investigate how meaningful living functions as a mediator between boredom, self-transcendence, and desperation. Of the 351 persons who took part in the study, 239 (68.1%) were women, and 112 (31.9%) were men. The participants’ average age was 21.92, SD=4.38. The study employed Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). Meaningful living plays a significant mediating role in the link between self-transcendence and boredom. Similarly, it was discovered that the relationship between self-transcendence and state desperation was fully mediated by meaningful living. Between boredom and state desperation, a positive correlation was discovered. Meaningful living and self-transcendence were found to be positively correlated, while boredom and state desperation were found to be negatively correlated.
